rationale: England have won the men's artistic team gold at the last three Commonwealth Games (2022 margin 13+ points over Canada); no evidence of a change in pecking order, though full-strength team in Glasgow 2026 is not confirmed.

Qualification round is often a formality throw; Pathirage is 2026 world leader (92.62m at Rome DL) and the kind of athlete who goes big early, Peters threw 86.08m in Rabat and confirmed CWG plans, while Nadeem/Chopra are coming back from injury/niggle and may throw conservatively to qualify.

Star-studded field: Nadeem is defending CWG champion (90.18m in 2022) and Olympic gold, Pathirage is 2026 world leader at 92.62m, world champion Walcott and 86.08m-throwing Peters are all confirmed; Nadeem's limited 2026 racing and Chopra's back injury/non-qualification risk temper their odds.

Without Australia/New Zealand the field is China (2025 Asia Cup runners-up), Philippines (2022 gold), Japan (host, strongest-ever B.League lineup) and Korea; a games-shaped bronze match could well be one of Japan/China losing a tight semifinal.
Yu Yiting set the Asian record 2:06.82 (world #1) at June 2026 Chinese Nationals, beating Yu Zidi (2:09.33) by 2.5s; Narita/Ye Shiwen/Kim are well behind on 2026 form.

Yu Zidi is the 2026 Asian leader at 4:30.79 (Chinese Nationals, June 19) with Ke Wenxi next at 4:33.59; Yu Yiting's best is 4:35.44 and could prioritise the 200 IM, though China's internal selection is uncertain.

Hou Zhihui is the class of the 49kg field (Olympic 49kg champion, 203kg at 2025 National Games) with no North Korean lifter entered at the May 2026 Asian Championships; Mirabai Chanu (205kg+ total, targeting 49kg at Asiad) is the main challenger and Rira Suzuki the home hope, but China's single-entry selection is unresolved.

Qin is world record holder and defending Asian Games 200m breast champion; Dong Zhihao showed 2026 form (58.57 100 breast, winning it over Qin at Chinese Nationals) and could be picked in the 200m, while Japan's Shin Ohashi (WJR 2:06.91) is a threat if entered.

Wide-open: Tada won the June 2026 Japanese title in 10.17 at the Asiad stadium with Shiraishi third (10.24) and neither Sakai nor Yanagita selected; Southeast Asian (Puripol Boonson) and Chinese sprinters (Lin Jianhao 10.11) are competitive but no single favourite exists.

Only Korea (Kang Dong-shin/RED231, winner of KeSPA selection events) and Japan (10-year-old prodigy Yuuki, 2026 GigaCrysta Grand Prix and Asia Esports Expo champion) have clearly identified elite Puyo Puyo singles reps; Japan has historically been the strongest Puyo Puyo nation, with Korea and Chinese Taipei the other contenders.

Sindhu (world #18) is unseeded-ish but has reached the last eight of majors consistently; An Se-young (0-10 H2H, including June 2026 Indonesia Open) and Wang Zhiyi/Yamaguchi block the final, so quarter/semifinal exit is most likely.
Sivasangari (world #5, defending Asiad champion, Malaysian gold target) is the top Asian woman; home player Satomi Watanabe (world #6) beat world #1 El Hammamy this season and is her main threat.

Ng Eain Yow (world #18, defending Asiad men's champion, Malaysian medal target, Olympic qualification at stake) is the clear top-ranked Asian male; Hong Kong's Lau Tsz Kwan (2025 Asian champion) and India's Abhay Singh/retiring Ghosal are the next tier.

Defending Asian Games champion and Asian record holder Nadeem, still the top-ranked Asian thrower, faces 2026 world leader Pathirage (92.62m) and an injury-returning Chopra; Japan's best (Sakiyama 81.78m) is far back.

China's U-23 squad reached the 2026 U-23 Asian Cup final but Japan thrashed them 4-0 in the final and send a strong U-21 side at home; Korea are the traditional Asiad football power and China is unlikely to take gold, so being knocked out by a Japanese or Korean side is most probable.
